<LOCKED_0001>
Fibres of <ACCENT_0001>tale morphisms.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme over a field <MATH_0002>.
The structure morphism <MATH_0003> is <ACCENT_0002>tale if
and only if <MATH_0004> is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable
field extensions of <MATH_0005>.
<STRUCT_0003> If <MATH_0006> is an <ACCENT_0003>tale morphism, then for every <MATH_0007> the
fibre <MATH_0008> is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field
extensions of <MATH_0009>.
<STRUCT_0004>

You can deduce this from Lemma <REF_0001>
via Lemma <REF_0002> above.
Here is a direct proof.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
We will use Algebra, Lemma <REF_0003>.
Hence it is clear that if <MATH_0001> is a disjoint union of spectra of finite
separable field extensions of <MATH_0002> then <MATH_0003> is <ACCENT_0001>tale.
Conversely, suppose that <MATH_0004> is <ACCENT_0002>tale. Then for any affine
open <MATH_0005> we see that <MATH_0006> is a finite disjoint union of spectra
of finite separable field extensions of <MATH_0007>. Hence all points of <MATH_0008>
are closed points (see
Lemma <REF_0004>
for example). Thus <MATH_0009> is a discrete space and we win.

The following lemma characterizes an <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism as a
flat, finitely presented morphism with ``<ACCENT_0002>tale fibres''.
